content: Citronellol, also known as dihydrogeraniol, is a naturally occurring acyclic monoterpenoid. Both enantiomers of citronellol are found in nature. The (+)-citronellol enantiomer is more commonly encountered and is present in citronella oils, such as those derived from Cymbopogon nardus, where it constitutes approximately 50% of the oil's composition. On the other hand, the (−)-citronellol enantiomer is predominantly found in rose oils, where it can make up 18-55% of the oil, as well as in geranium oils. Citronellol is widely utilized in the formulation of perfumes and insect repellents. Additionally, it serves as an attractant for mites in certain applications. From a health and safety perspective, the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has classified citronellol as GRAS (Generally Recognized as Safe) for use in food products.
